problem: If $sin⁡\theta =-\frac{1}{5}$ and ${270}^{∘}<\theta <{360}^{∘}$ then what is the value of $cos⁡\theta ?$

feedback.problem: If $sin⁡\theta =\frac{5}{13}$ and $\frac{\pi }{2}<\theta <\pi $ then what is the value of $cos⁡\theta ?$
feedback.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932638/assets/d6ec4c0b71e64cd659bceea63a49f0ef09c44ee1c31353fd377963d7cdf3c3db.png)

We're given that $sin⁡\theta =\frac{5}{13}.$ We can use the Pythagorean identity to find $cos⁡\theta :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1 \\ {cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ cos⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $sin⁡\theta =\frac{5}{13}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}cos⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{(\frac{5}{13})}^{2}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{1-\frac{25}{169}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{144}{169}} \\  & =\pm \frac{12}{13}.\end{aligned}
$$

We select the negative answer since $cos⁡\theta $ is negative in the second quadrant. So, $cos⁡\theta =-\frac{12}{13}.$
